edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.population: adults using loop or thiazide diuretics
edges.mechanism: This drug-related edge is biologically plausible because the medication changes absorption, excretion, endocrine signaling, or tissue turnover in a predictable direction. Duration, dose, and co-medication use usually determine whether the effect becomes clinically relevant for Magnesium deficiency.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link loop or thiazide diuretic use to higher risk of magnesium deficiency in adults using loop or thiazide diuretics. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
